task.name: Workflow Permission Drift Remediation
task.description: Review covered GitHub Actions workflows after workflow or policy changes and surface only workflows whose declared permissions exceed the repository operator's approved minimum permission profile without an already tracked or explicitly accepted exception.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent discovering and correcting excessive workflow token permissions while avoiding duplicate attention on permission drift that is already tracked or explicitly accepted.
activationConditions: A pull request merged within the evidence window changes a workflow file, reusable workflow reference, or repository workflow-permissions policy in a covered repository.
Authoritative repository workflow evidence shows at least one covered workflow now declares a permission set broader than the approved minimum permission profile for its role.
requiredEffects: Each novel permission-drift finding identifies the affected workflow, the excessive declared permission scope, the approved minimum permission profile, and the authoritative repository evidence supporting the determination.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding using repository-linked evidence.
noopConditions: No changed covered workflow declares permissions broader than its approved minimum permission profile.
Every supported workflow-permission-drift finding for the changed covered workflows is already tracked or explicitly accepted.
successConditions: Supported workflow-permission-drift findings receive accepted remediation evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days of the workflow run.
Workflow changes whose declared permissions already satisfy the approved minimum profile create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: A documented temporary exception may intentionally allow one workflow to retain broader permissions for a bounded migration period while still requiring explicit acceptance evidence.
One workflow can exceed the approved minimum profile in more than one permission scope and therefore produce more than one supported finding.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel workflow-permission-drift findings assigned to the run that are resolved or explicitly dismissed within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported workflow-permission-drift findings it assigns for changed covered workflows.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request that narrows the identified workflow's declared permissions to the approved minimum profile before the evidence cutoff.
A closed tracking issue, pull request conversation, or repository-linked exception record that explicitly marks the permission-drift finding resolved, dismissed, or accepted by a maintainer.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran.

metric.name: resolved-supported-permission-drift-findings
metric.formula: resolved-or-dismissed supported permission-drift findings / supported novel workflow-permission-drift findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel workflow-permission-drift finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned workflow-permission-drift finding set or required repository workflow permission evidence for the changed covered workflows cannot be read.
